samples.summary: applyBorderPatch writes cells through compactCell, which silently drops spill metadata (spillAnchor/spillRows/spillCols/spillBlocked)
samples.evidence: `const newCell = compactCell(cell, style)` (sheet.ts:4029). `compactCell` (style-mutation.ts:53-65) copies ONLY `v`, `f` and `s`; `Cell` also carries `spillRows`, `spillCols`, `spillAnchor`, `spillBlocked` (model/core/types.ts:209-217), and YorkieStore.normalizeCell (frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:228-239) does persist them, so the loss is caused here. `collectBorderTargets` (sheet.ts:4043-4056) enumerates every cell in the selection with no read-only skip — contrast toggleCheckboxesInRange, which explicitly skips `cell?.f || cell?.spillAnchor` (sheet.ts:3906). Consequences of applying e.g. 'all borders' over a spilled array: (a) a ghost cell loses `spillAnchor`, so the next recalculation treats it as user data and blocks the spill with #REF! (calculator.ts:109-125); (b) the spill anchor loses `spillRows`/`spillCols`, so setData's ghost-cleanup contract (sheet.ts:1003-1008) never fires and stale ghosts are orphaned. The same defect exists in `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3679), so it is pre-existing behavior — but this change re-implements the write inline and is the border path's new write site, and the cheap fix (`{...cell}` spread instead of compactCell, or skipping ghost/anchor cells) belongs here.

samples.summary: Pruning decides once, at apply time, so a border layer added later resurfaces on cells the user explicitly cleared
samples.evidence: `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys(range, normalized, this.getStyleSources())` (sheet.ts:4003) only keeps a `false` when a conflicting sheet/col/row/range layer EXISTS AT THAT MOMENT (hasConflictingStyleSourceForKey, style-mutation.ts:200-248). Before this change the border path stored the explicit `false` unconditionally, so a cleared cell stayed border-free even when a column/row/sheet border was introduced afterwards (setRangeStyle's column branch, sheet.ts:3695-3705, writes the column style without touching cell-level overrides). After this change the cleared key is gone, so `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:881) lets the later layer paint a border back onto that cell. Reachable via xlsx import column/row borders and any setRangeStyle carrying border keys (view/spreadsheet.ts:223). Likely an accepted trade-off (it matches the range-style path), but it is a real behavior change not covered by any test.

samples.summary: New store.delete path removes an existing cell without dependant recalculation or filter refresh
samples.evidence: `await this.store.delete(anchor)` (sheet.ts:4031) is newly reachable from the border flow: in `setStyle` the equivalent branch (sheet.ts:3680) is dead because `mergeStylePatch` never returns an empty style for a non-empty patch, so setRangeBorders previously only ever wrote. A cell holding `v: ''` plus border-only style is now deleted (isEmptyCell treats `v:''` as no content, style-mutation.ts:44-48) with no `buildDependantsMap`/`calculate` and no `recomputeFilterHiddenRows`, unlike every other cell-removing path (cf. toggleCheckboxesInRange, sheet.ts:3928-3934). COUNTBLANK-style semantics appear to treat `v:''` and a missing cell identically (test/formula/formula.test.ts:543-549), so the observable impact is probably nil — flagging it because nothing in the change or tests establishes that.

samples.summary: setRangeBorders still returns true when every key pruned away and nothing was written
samples.evidence: `return true` (sheet.ts:3968) is unconditional, while applyBorderPatch can now legitimately do nothing at all (early returns at 4022 and 4026). view/spreadsheet.ts:244 uses the boolean as 'something changed' to drive a repaint. Harmless (an empty batch is discarded by YorkieStore.endBatch, yorkie-store.ts:1171, so no dead undo step), but the return value no longer means what the caller reads it as.

finding.summary: applyBorderPatch writes cells through compactCell, which silently drops spill metadata (spillAnchor/spillRows/spillCols/spillBlocked)
finding.evidence: `const newCell = compactCell(cell, style)` (sheet.ts:4029). `compactCell` (style-mutation.ts:53-65) copies ONLY `v`, `f` and `s`; `Cell` also carries `spillRows`, `spillCols`, `spillAnchor`, `spillBlocked` (model/core/types.ts:209-217), and YorkieStore.normalizeCell (frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:228-239) does persist them, so the loss is caused here. `collectBorderTargets` (sheet.ts:4043-4056) enumerates every cell in the selection with no read-only skip — contrast toggleCheckboxesInRange, which explicitly skips `cell?.f || cell?.spillAnchor` (sheet.ts:3906). Consequences of applying e.g. 'all borders' over a spilled array: (a) a ghost cell loses `spillAnchor`, so the next recalculation treats it as user data and blocks the spill with #REF! (calculator.ts:109-125); (b) the spill anchor loses `spillRows`/`spillCols`, so setData's ghost-cleanup contract (sheet.ts:1003-1008) never fires and stale ghosts are orphaned. The same defect exists in `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3679), so it is pre-existing behavior — but this change re-implements the write inline and is the border path's new write site, and the cheap fix (`{...cell}` spread instead of compactCell, or skipping ghost/anchor cells) belongs here.

verdict.reason: The code exists exactly as described. applyBorderPatch (sheet.ts:4029) rewrites the whole cell via compactCell, which copies only v/f/s (style-mutation.ts:53-65), while Cell also carries spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor/spillBlocked (types.ts:209-217). Both stores replace the cell wholesale (memory.ts:97-100; yorkie-store.ts:213-254,259-275), so the spill metadata is lost on persist. collectBorderTargets (sheet.ts:4037-4059) iterates every cell in the selection with no ghost/anchor skip — unlike the checkbox path which explicitly skips cell?.f || cell?.spillAnchor (sheet.ts:3906) — so applying a border preset over a spilled array is a reachable path. Losing spillAnchor makes the next recalculation treat the ghost as user data and block the spill with #REF! (calculator.ts:101-125); losing spillRows/spillCols on the anchor defeats the ghost-cleanup contract in calculator.ts:74-85 and setData sheet.ts:1003-1019, orphaning stale ghosts. No caller-side guard prevents this: setRangeBorders (sheet.ts:3945-3969) only checks selection type and a cell-count cap. Real, in-lane (data loss / broken invariant), and blocking.
